async/await: Current State

SLA already has async fn/.await syntax and the accompanying sa_std future contracts. The current compiler already generates real state machines for a single await, two consecutive awaits, join2, and several dynamic Pending/Ready forms; but this is not "all async code already has a general runtime". This page records the verifiable lowering scope, the manual driving method, and the boundaries still unfinished.

Source snapshot (2026-09-03) The authoritative implementation lives in sa_plugin_sla, not in this help site itself: src/codegen.zig selects a dedicated constructor in the order join2 → two-await → single-await → dynamic planner; sa_std/core/future.sal defines FutureState's dynamic vtable at offset +48, and dynamic state must be dispatched through FUTURE_POLL_STATE. Do not hand a dynamic outer future to FUTURE_READY_POLL_STATE, which only reads the inline ready layout.

Basic spelling

async fn declares an asynchronous function; calling it yields a future value, and the suffix .await takes the result. A future's type is written future<T> (demos/rosetta/314_async_await_pending_resume/main.sla):

@import "sa_std/future.sa"
@import "sa_std/core/waker.sa"
@import "sa_std/pin.sa"
@import "sa_std/core/box.sa"

async fn step_value(x: i32) -> i32 {
    let v = future::defer_ready(x).await;
    return v * 2;
}

async fn run() -> i32 {
    let first = step_value(10).await;
    let second = step_value(first + 1).await;
    return second;
}

Pending / Ready and manual block_on

future::defer_ready(v) returns Pending on the first poll and Ready(v) on the second — this makes the async state machine genuinely suspend and resume on re-poll. When the standard library has no built-in block_on, the demo uses a handwritten driver of polling + waker:

fn block_on(future: future<i32>) -> i32 {
    let data: ptr = PTR_NULL();
    let raw = RAW_WAKER_NEW(data, data);
    let waker = WAKER_FROM_RAW(raw);
    let context = CONTEXT_FROM_WAKER(waker);
    let boxed = Box::new(future);
    let future_ref = *boxed;
    let pinned = stack_alloc();
    PIN_MUT_NEW(pinned, future_ref);

    while unix_now_ns() < deadline {
        let poll = FUTURE_POLL_STATE(PIN_MUT_GET_MUT(pinned), context);
        let ready = POLL_IS_READY(poll);
        if ready == true {
            let value: i32 = POLL_VALUE(poll);
            return value;
        };
        THREAD_SLEEP_MS(1);
    }
    panic(314);
}

A cross-thread task pool

Futures produced by async calls can be moved into a thread closure and driven by the worker thread itself; results are returned through an Arc<Mutex<i32>> (demos/rosetta/315_async_thread_pool/main.sla):

@import "sa_std/sync/mutex.sa"
@import "sa_std/core/arc.sa"
@import "sa_std/thread.sa"

fn get_cell(c: Arc<Mutex<i32> >) -> i32 {
    let g = (*c).lock().unwrap();
    return *g;
}

fn pool_worker(f: future<i32>, out: Arc<Mutex<i32> >) {
    let r = block_on(f);
    let g = (*out).lock().unwrap();
    *g = r;
}

The while let + await combination

The common form of a task queue (demos/rosetta/136_executor_task_queue/main.sla):

let queue = vec(task_one(), task_two(), task_three());
let total = 0;

while let Some(task) = queue.pop() {
    let resolved = task.await;
    total = total + resolved;
}

Maturity and recommendations

  • async/await has partially entered the direct-SAB fast path, but the coverage is dedicated lowering, not a general CPS/state-machine for arbitrary async functions. What is currently verified focuses on a single await, two awaits, join2, local Future reassignment, and Pending/Ready resumption;
  • In the current source record, 34 test_unit_async*.sla pass on native SA, and the SLA→SA→VM matrix is also 34/34; the 2026-09-29 re-check found strict direct SAB likewise 34/34 (the thread-pool case turned green after alignment through the helpers gate, sa_plugin_sla@f5f473b). The earlier "34/35, the thread pool limited by the stack_alloc + PIN_MUT_NEW + FUTURE_POLL_STATE combination" was the 2026-09-03 snapshot and has been superseded;
  • Linear consecutive awaits are now general: the three-await case (test_unit_async_linear_three_await_state_machine, resuming over four poll rounds) passes in the tree; a four-await probe (four-stage local values a+b+c+d=44 kept across stages) also passes. What is still missing is nested awaits across async fn boundaries: rosetta 314/315 still fail with assertion panics (a shared-layer gap, see below). Do not claim on this basis that "advanced async/await is complete";
  • The executor in sa_std/core/task.sa is a polling loop over a task array; run_until_complete has no Tokio-grade reactor, scheduling fairness, backpressure, or structured concurrency. The thread-pool example uses real OS threads + Arc<Mutex>, but is still driven by a handwritten block_on and sleeps;
  • Demo 009's simplified block_on panics when the future is not immediately ready; for genuine suspension, refer to demo 314's polling spelling;
  • Do not assume all async demos in the rosetta tree pass end to end; verify individually as needed: SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla test demos/rosetta/314_async_await_pending_resume/main.sla.
  • Measured on 2026-09-29: 22 spot-checked demos (enum/match, closures, trait/dyn, iterators, Cell/RefCell, Box, derive, select/join/streams, basic async) produced completely identical output on both backends; rosetta 314/315 panic identically on both backends (nested awaits across async fn boundaries, a shared-layer gap, not an SA/SAB divergence; a separate project);
  • Panic propagation across future / await boundaries (TS-16, written 2026-10-29): a panic() inside an async body is symmetric with the goroutine boundary position — process-level termination, not observed by the future in data form: the future's state / polling representation (sa_std/future.sa) has no panic slot, poll never returns a "panicked" result, and the process terminates directly at the poll driving point (the interpreted path records it as RunError.UserExit, the compiled path as the panic / panic_msg host calls).
NoteThe compiler internally uses continuation/state-machine lowering, but SLA provides no Rust-style Pin/Unpin user-facing semantics; the PIN_MUT_* appearing in demos comes from sa_std contracts, not from language keywords. The HTTP client's async ABI is currently a handle + poll/cancel plugin interface and cannot be equated with a unified SLA Future executor.

Related pages: Functions and Control Flow, Feature Maturity Matrix.
